description: Georgia law requires actual notice to parents before an abortion on an unemancipated minor. What remedies exist if the abortion doctor fails to comply?
shortAnswer: The burden is on the abortion doctor to prove the parents or guardians were notified and the minor signed a consent form. Unfortunately, there is no private cause of action (right to sue) against abortion doctors provided for within the statute itself. My firm is willing to sue abortion doctors over this issue under the right circumstances.

faq.q: What does Georgia's parental notification law require before a minor's abortion?
faq.a: Unemancipated minors seeking an abortion must either be accompanied by a parent or guardian who can show proper identification or a minor's parent or guardian must be notified in person, by telephone, or by mail at least 24 hours prior to the abortion. The law requires "actual notice" to the parents or guardians.

faq.q: Can Georgia's parental notification requirement be waived?
faq.a: If the physician or minor does not want to comply with these parental notification requirements, he or she can contact any juvenile court in the state to have them waived. Regardless of whether parental notification occurs, a minor is required to sign a form stating that she consents freely, "and without coercion" to the abortion.

faq.q: Can I sue for wrongful death if an abortion doctor did not notify me before my daughter's abortion?
faq.a: At this time, there is no law in Georgia that allows a woman or the parent of a minor to sue for wrongful death of an aborted child when the abortion doctor fails to prove "notice and consent." The right case may allow us to use existing laws to hold abortion doctors legally responsible for not complying.

faq.q: What happened to the Women's Private Right of Action Bill in Georgia?
faq.a: In 2011 the Georgia Senate passed a bill that would allow women (and a minor's parent or legal guardian) to sue an abortion practitioner for violating the Woman's Right To Know Act. Unfortunately, Georgia's House leadership blocked the legislation by refusing to allow it a committee hearing.
